pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an underlying Ovarian Teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic ultrasound demonstrating a mature cystic ovarian teratoma with CSF positive for IgG antibodies targeting the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The underlying ovarian teratoma contains ectopic neural tissue expressing NMDA receptors. The patient's immune system mounts an antibody response against these foreign-appearing neural antigens, specifically targeting the GluN1 subunit of NMDA receptors. These autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and cause cross-linking and selective internalization of surface NMDA receptors in forebrain and hippocampal neurons. The resulting hypofunction of NMDA receptors leads to loss of GABAergic inhibition, precipitating a catastrophic cascade of psychiatric psychosis, catatonia, bizarre orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic breakdown, and life-threatening hypoventilation. Treatment requires urgent surgical resection of the teratoma alongside aggressive immunotherapy (corticosteroids, IVIG/plasma exchange, and rituximab).
